questions.text: Marine engineering subjects in this course are divided into which two broad areas?
options: Engineering of marine activities topside & engineering of marine activities underwater

questions.text: Which activity is NOT a topside activity?
options: ROV intervention on a subsea valve
Structural installation of an offshore platform from the deck

questions.text: Which of the following is a typical underwater engineering activity?
Primary reason for performing a survey before design/installation is to:
options: Shorten project schedule by skipping design reviews
Confirm the site is adequate and safe for the intended system

questions.text: Offshore survey contractors typically:
options: Provide and operate vessel positioning systems and signals

questions.text: Pre-design information for a fixed jacket site commonly includes all EXCEPT:
options: Existing seabed facilities near the location

questions.text: Why are offshore surveys often very expensive?
options: All survey gear is disposable by regulation
The underwater environment makes data gathering complex and resource-intensive

questions.text: Visual survey typically involves:
options: Human/Camera observation via ROV/AUV or divers

questions.text: Depth survey methods commonly include:
An echo sounder determines depth by:
options: Measuring light reflectivity of the seabed
Transmitting a sound pulse from the surface and timing its return from the seabed
Weighing a drop weight on the bottom

questions.text: Because seabeds are rarely flat, echo sounders provide:
options: A full 3D model of all buried layers
Instantaneous depth at a point beneath the transducer
Only average depth along a transect

questions.text: Which relation is correct for sound in water during echo sounding?
A subsea depth profiler primarily provides:
options: Information on layers below the seabed
Wave height at the free surface only

questions.text: One principle behind depth/sub-bottom profiling is to detect:
options: Color changes visible to the naked eye
Conductivity or electromagnetic differences between layers

questions.text: Which task needs MORE detailed depth profiling?
options: Piling for a slot jacket platform

questions.text: Combining echo sounding with sub-bottom profiling allows engineers to:
options: Generate seabed contours AND understand sub-seabed layers

questions.text: Compared to a basic echo sounder, a sub-bottom profiler:
options: Penetrates the seafloor to reflect from deeper strata
Uses only magnetic fields and no acoustics

questions.text: Integrating GPS with survey acquisition allows you to:
options: Tag each data point/image with position coordinates

questions.text: A sea-bottom (seabed) survey is performed primarily to:
options: Confirm the site is free of obstructions such as wrecks or existing assets
Verify cafeteria menus on the barge

questions.text: Marine magnetometers are used to detect:
options: Ferrous objects and magnetic anomalies on/within the seabed

questions.text: Why is a surface-towed magnetometer streamed far behind the ship?
options: To minimize interference from the ship’s own magnetic field
To stay within visual range of divers
Because it has no power cable
To keep it in shallow water only

questions.text: Compared with deep-towed magnetometers, surface-towed units generally:
options: Cover larger areas at lower cost but with less detail
Cannot be used in salt water

questions.text: 3D imaging of subsea assets can be achieved using:
options: Laser scanning, fibre-optic, ultrasonic, and acoustic imaging

questions.text: A key advantage of 3D imaging mentioned is that it can be used for:
Which is a listed disadvantage of 3D imaging systems?
options: They inevitably contain some measurement errors and can be expensive

questions.text: Positioning for offshore surveys commonly starts from:
options: Random local benchmarks with no tie-in

questions.text: In survey terminology, a global grid refers to:
options: X/Y measured only on the vessel deck

questions.text: Why might an onshore communications dish be part of the positioning chain?
options: To boost communication between satellites, the vessel, and survey tools

questions.text: An as-built survey is performed to:
options: Document actual installation geometry after field deviations

questions.text: A common cause of deviations captured by as-built surveys is:
options: Wave and sea-load challenges leading to practical compromises

questions.text: What is the most compelling reason for adopting subsea processing in deepwater developments?
Among conventional artificial-lift systems, which is closest in principle to subsea processing?
Why can gas-lift performance deteriorate as more gas is injected?
options: Flow-induced friction losses overtake density benefits

questions.text: Gas lift does NOT improve which of the following, limiting its use for certain layouts?
Benchmark data show superior deepwater economics mainly come from:
options: Higher production/reserves per well and processing at an existing host

questions.text: The first prototype seabed separation unit was tested:
options: In 1989 on Argyll field, North Sea
In 1969 on the Zakum field, offshore Abu Dhabi
In 1978 in the Gulf of Mexico

questions.text: The Highlander/Tartan subsea slug catcher was installed primarily to overcome:
BOET’s prototype SSPU (1989) featured:
options: Two-stage system with three-phase horizontal separators

questions.text: Kvaerner Booster Station (KBS) included which combination?
options: Two-phase vertical centrifugal separator, axial gas compressor, liquid centrifugal pump
Horizontal gravity separator and reciprocating pump

questions.text: A unique feature of the VASPS concept was that the unit:
options: Was mounted on a surface platform
Fit inside a 30-in surface casing of a 'dummy' well
Eliminated the need for any riser

questions.text: The AlphaPrime concept emphasized:
options: Self-contained retrievable process modules with detachable lines and all-electric power

questions.text: The Troll C Pilot (SUBSIS) was designed to:
options: Reinject oil and vent gas subsea
Remove water subsea and pipe gas+oil to platform

questions.text: Which capacity figure best describes the Troll Pilot horizontal separator?
For deepwater subsea vessels, a key structural design criterion is:
Which environmental factors most challenge subsea processing designs?
options: Rapid heat loss, long flowlines, tall risers

questions.text: In two-phase separation design, the limiting parameter is usually gas rate controlled by:
For fluids with high foaming tendency subsea, the preferred approach is:
options: Passive mechanical foam-breaking (low-shear inlet) over chemical injection

questions.text: To mitigate hydrate risks subsea, operators commonly use:
options: Methanol and ethylene glycol; only methanol can break existing hydrates

questions.text: The only sure way to prevent wax deposition in cold subsea pipelines is to:
For severe slugging in offshore pipelines/risers, the most dependable solution today is:
A subsea pig launcher is used primarily to:
options: Insert cleaning/scraping devices to control deposits inside pipelines

questions.text: Compact cyclone separators are attractive subsea because they:
options: Rely on gravity and large volumes
Use centrifugal acceleration to reduce vessel size and have no moving parts

questions.text: Preferred sand-handling philosophy offshore (for steady, small fines) is to:
options: Keep solids suspended and moving to shore; consider erosion-resistant liners

questions.text: Which pump type most often meets subsea high-flow, high-head service?
Compared with water-turbine drives, electric-motor pump drives subsea typically:
options: Enable variable-speed control but require high-voltage power
Cannot be used below 100 m water depth

questions.text: A continuing challenge for subsea power is developing reliable mateable connectors at approximately:
options: 11 kV and higher (with concepts up to ~36 kV)

questions.text: Subsea power distribution must provide different voltage levels primarily for:
All-electric valve actuators are attractive subsea because they:
options: Are depth-insensitive and avoid complex hydraulics

questions.text: A 'wet tree' differs from a 'dry tree' mainly in that it is:
options: Installed on the seabed and typically operated via ROVs/remote control
Installed topside for direct crew access

questions.text: Which statement best describes subsea manifolds and risers?
options: Manifolds gather effluent from trees; risers are the pipeline sections that rise to surface and often have thicker walls due to hydrodynamic loads
Manifolds only support ROV docking; risers are thinner than pipelines
Manifolds separate oil and gas; risers are jumpers

questions.text: In this course, corrosion is defined primarily as:
options: The destructive reaction of a material with its environment
A reversible physical change in crystal structure
Only rusting in air without moisture
A manufacturing defect unrelated to environment

questions.text: Which pair most strongly accelerates corrosion in marine conditions?
A correct statement about oxidation in metals in this context is:
options: It always produces hydrogen gas directly
It can be described as a gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen
It never occurs in the presence of water
It is unrelated to redox reactions

questions.text: Which statement about corrosion films is TRUE?
options: All corrosion films are uniformly protective
Aluminum can form protective films, while mild steel films are usually destructive
Steel always passivates in seawater without coatings
Films only form in the absence of oxygen

questions.text: Which is NOT listed as a type of corrosion in these notes?
According to the rule of thumb given, when soil resistivity is greater than about 3000 Ω·cm, the preferred CP method is:
Cathodic protection works primarily by:
options: Raising the metal’s temperature above seawater temperature
Supplying electrons to the structure to suppress anodic dissolution

questions.text: In sacrificial-anode CP for a steel structure, which role pairing is correct?
options: Steel and Mg are both anodes

questions.text: A required condition for CP to function properly is the presence of:
Which paint system description is correct?
options: 2-coat: two topcoats only; 3-coat: primer + two primers

questions.text: Corrosion prevention should be considered:
options: From the design/conception stage through operation

questions.text: Erosion-related corrosion mechanisms highlighted include:
IMR activities are primarily carried out:
options: After installation to ensure continued fitness for service
Only after full failure of a system

questions.text: In these notes, the purpose of inspection is best summarized as:
options: To reduce taxes on offshore assets
To reconfirm that facilities behave as designed and detect deviations

questions.text: Two broad classes of inspection discussed are:
Which is listed as an example of destructive testing?
Which are classed as visual inspection in the notes?
Under the 'sounds' category, NDT modalities mentioned include:
Eddy-current testing detects flaws by using:
Magnetic Flux Leakage (MFL) is widely used to detect:
options: Corrosion and pitting in steel structures

questions.text: Condition monitoring under preventive maintenance commonly uses:
options: Fibre-optic, pressure, vibration, and temperature sensors

questions.text: Corrective maintenance is undertaken when:
options: There are no symptoms at all
Equipment begins to show signs of impending failure

questions.text: A listed pipeline repair method is:
Rehabilitation vs. modification is best described as:
options: Both always replace the full system with a new one
Rehabilitation adapts to new operating regimes; modification is like-for-like
Rehabilitation is like-for-like restoration; modification adapts capacity for new regimes

questions.text: Commercial diving refers to:
SCUBA diving is characterized by:
options: Bottled breathing gas without continuous surface supply
Only helium as a breathing medium

questions.text: According to the table, Nitrox I composition is approximately:
In the dive community, 'trimix' refers to blends of:
The naming convention 'trimix 20/30' indicates:
Saturation diving involves:
options: Keeping divers at ambient surface pressure throughout
Diver tissues being saturated with inert gases while living under pressure
Only using air with no mixed gas

questions.text: A 'closed bell' enables which critical procedure?
options: Transfer Under Pressure (TUP) to deck chambers

questions.text: A key hazard typically beyond ~30 m in air diving is:
Ear pain on descent is primarily due to:
options: Increasing outside pressure relative to middle ear
Decreasing oxygen fraction in the lungs

questions.text: Decompression (DECO) is conducted to:
options: Allow dissolved inert gases to leave tissues safely over time

questions.text: Compared to SCUBA, surface-supplied diving provides:
options: Breathing gas umbilical and often better control/support from the surface

questions.text: A 'slow ascend' (SA) in these notes refers to:
options: Returning rapidly to surface to reduce cold exposure
A controlled, slower return aiding safe decompression
A sprint to the surface to conserve gas

questions.text: An ROV is typically:
options: A remotely operated, tethered vehicle controlled from a surface ship

questions.text: An AUV such as ABE is best used for:
options: Real-time manual manipulations requiring pilot feedback
Pre-programmed surveys and mapping missions without supervision

questions.text: ROPOS is controlled via:
options: Acoustic pings only with onboard power
Fibre-optic tether providing power and real-time data/video

questions.text: A valve pack on an ROV primarily contains:
options: Directional control valves (DCVs) that actuate cylinders
